I made one change to `0.html`, and it is untested in a browser. The check for a local Chrome to render it was blocked, because this session can only access the working directory.

## The change

Multi-paragraph list items (the kind Markdown produces) had no space between them, while paragraphs *inside* an item were 1rem apart. The rule that strips the bottom margin from the last child of an `li` caused this. I added at `0.html:107`:

```css
li:has(> p) + li, li + li:has(> p) {
  margin-block-start: 1rem;
}
```

Lists without paragraphs are unaffected.

## What I left alone

I reviewed the rest of the stylesheet and found nothing else worth changing.

Two things I can't improve without your input:

- **Placeholder content:** the title and `<h1>` are both `0`, and there is no `<meta name="description">`. I didn't invent content.
- **Scrollable tables:** `table { display: block }` makes wide tables scroll without a wrapper element, but older Safari versions drop table semantics for screen readers when it's set. The more robust alternative is a wrapper `<div>` with `overflow-x: auto`, which means a markup change wherever a table is used. The page has no tables yet, so I left it.

If you had a different kind of improvement in mind (visual design, real content, a colour palette), tell me the direction and I'll take it there.
